findings.claim: The course intake's Concept-day allocation for S20 (authoring/evidence/html-css-js/intake.md, section Block allocation per day) schedules topic videos only in the 8-minute Short video block, 'topic videos whose runtimes sum to 8 minutes or less across the day (a video that does not fit is recorded absent with the reason)'. The four S20 companions assign 7.30 (semantic), 2.22 (forms), 7.57 (accessibility) and 8.37 (box model) optional watch minutes, 25.46 minutes in all, so at most one or two of them fit the block. This 2.22-minute video is the one S20 companion that comfortably fits; the problem is day-level, not with this file.
findings.recommendation: Keep this video as the S20 scheduled video when the day-level choice is made, and record that choice so the other S20 companions are clearly marked as unscheduled or absent per the intake.

findings.claim: The creator description carries no timestamp chapters and the player metadata exposes none, yet the companion says the coverage and its minute ranges come 'Per its chapters, description and captions' and the cautions say fit was judged from 'the chapters'. A learner or reviewer cannot tell where the segment boundaries come from.
findings.recommendation: Say where the time ranges come from (YouTube auto-generated key moments, or caption timestamps) and drop 'chapters' wherever the creator published none, in both the body line and the cautions.

findings.claim: Objective o1 has two parts: a visible associated label, and an accessible name (aria-label) for a control with no visible label, such as the icon-only search button the page's label-fixer activity uses. The gaps list covers o2 and o3 only and the covers list mentions only implicit and explicit label association, so a learner is not told that the aria-label half of o1 is page-only.
findings.recommendation: Add an o1 gap line, for example 'o1: labels are shown; naming a control with no visible label (aria-label) is not covered; the page teaches it', unless the captions show the video does cover it.
